prompt: Why doesn't chlorobenzene undergo SNAr with NaOMe under mild conditions, while 2,4-dinitrochlorobenzene does?

options.label: The nitro groups stabilize the negatively-charged Meisenheimer intermediate via resonance
The nitro groups push the chlorine out, making the C-Cl bond easier to break
Nitro's inductive effect weakens the aromatic C-Cl bond enough for displacement
Nitro groups make the ring more polar, which attracts the methoxide more strongly

explanation: SNAr proceeds via a NEGATIVELY CHARGED Meisenheimer intermediate (Nu added, sp³ C still bearing Cl). Nitro groups ortho/para accept this negative charge by resonance — stabilizing the TS and intermediate. Chlorobenzene has no such stabilization; its Meisenheimer would be too high in energy.
